semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Windows Model Cache Cleanup
semantic_findings.description: Optional cleanup says to delete the model but gives the Windows path C:\Users\<name>\.cache\huggingface\hub. Deleting this shared directory could remove unrelated models.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The Windows alternative names the whole hub directory, unlike the model-specific Unix path. The deletion instruction therefore exposes unrelated cached models to removal.

content.user_title: Separate Video Subjects Locally with SAM 2.1
content.value_statement: Manual video subject masking can take substantial editing time. This skill guides local SAM 2.1 processing to generate frame masks and a green highlight preview.
actual_capabilities: Inspect local GPU availability and select a SAM 2.1 model for NVIDIA, Apple Silicon, or CPU processing.
Generate a coordinate-grid preview for selecting positive subject points and negative exclusion points.
Propagate one subject mask through a selected frame range using chunked video processing.
Save numbered binary PNG masks under work/masks/subject/.
Render work/separated.mp4 with a green subject highlight and source audio when available.
Guide point corrections after reviewing frames for missing subject areas or unwanted mask spill.
limitations: Requires Python 3.10+, ffmpeg, local package installation, and internet access for initial dependency and model downloads.
CPU processing can be slow; long clips require substantial time and mask storage.
The provided workflow handles one subject and requires constant frame rate video.
Masks are hard-edged, especially around hair; output is a green preview, not a transparent video or automatic background replacement.

use_cases.title: Prepare Masks for Video Compositing
use_cases.description: Generate subject masks from a short clip for later compositing in an external editor.

use_cases.title: Isolate Products from Handling
use_cases.description: Use exclusion points to keep hands, packaging, or a tabletop outside a product mask.

use_cases.title: Inspect Local Segmentation Results
use_cases.description: Create binary frame masks and inspect green overlays before reusing the masks in a separate analysis workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Short Subject Mask
prompt_templates.prompt: Use object-separation on clip.mp4. Separate the person in frames 0 through 19 and show the green preview before processing more frames.

prompt_templates.title: Separate a Product
prompt_templates.prompt: Separate the bottle in product.mp4, frames 30 through 89. Exclude the holding hand and table, then save the masks and preview.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: use positive and negative points.

prompt_templates.title: Plan for Limited Hardware
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect available hardware for interview.mp4 and report the selected model, download size, and expected speed. Wait for approval before installation or downloads.

prompt_templates.title: Refine and Export a Frame Range
prompt_templates.prompt: For demo.mp4 frames 100 through 219, test 20 frames first. Refine exclusion points around occlusions, then export masks and the green preview. Preserve existing outputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: validate difficult motion before full export.

output_examples.input: Separate the presenter in clip.mp4, frames 0 through 19.
output: Expected preview: work/separated.mp4, showing the presenter highlighted in green.
Expected masks: numbered PNG files in work/masks/subject/, with white pixels marking the subject.
Review the beginning, middle, and end before extending the selected range.

output_examples.input: Prepare a product mask without including the hand holding it.
output: Point plan: positive points inside the product and negative points on the hand and table.
Validation: inspect contact edges and occlusions in a short test range.
Expected deliverables: binary subject masks and a green highlight video; background replacement requires another editing step.

best_practices: Test about 20 frames and inspect occlusions before processing the full selected range.
Confirm download sizes and use a dedicated project directory; preserve existing outputs before rerunning.
Delete only confirmed skill-specific cache folders during cleanup, especially on Windows.
anti_patterns: Expecting the supplied renderer to produce transparent video or replace the background automatically.
Processing long CPU-only clips without estimating time or checking a short sample.
Deleting the entire shared Hugging Face cache to remove one downloaded model.

faq.question: Do I need a GPU?
faq.answer: No. The workflow selects a small model for CPU processing, but processing can take about five seconds per frame.

faq.question: Does the workflow upload my video?
faq.answer: The provided code processes video locally and contains no video upload operation. Initial setup downloads packages and model files.

faq.question: Which files does it produce?
faq.answer: It writes work/separated.mp4 with a green subject highlight and numbered binary masks under work/masks/subject/.

faq.question: Does it remove or replace the background?
faq.answer: Not in the provided renderer. It generates masks and a green preview; transparent export or background replacement needs an additional workflow.

faq.question: How does it handle hair and attached objects?
faq.answer: Masks are hard-edged and can miss fine hair. Add exclusion points for packaging or other attached objects, then review the result.

faq.question: What should I check before cleanup?
faq.answer: Keep needed outputs and confirm exact cache folders. The Windows cleanup path names a shared cache and could remove unrelated models.
